title: Digital Marketing
text: This page showcases my applied digital marketing work — from standing up a full measurement stack for a live brand launch, to auditing enterprise content systems, to analyzing competitive SEO landscapes. My target audience is marketing managers, agency directors, and academic search committees looking for a practitioner who can move between strategy and execution.

title: Digital Marketing
section: Rising Stars Muay Thai — Brand Launch & Campaign Analytics
text:
Rising Stars Muay Thai — Brand Launch & Campaign Analytics
I designed, built, and deployed the full website for Rising Stars Muay Thai and then ran an end-to-end digital analytics engagement across two live event cycles.

Web Development & Measurement Implementation

Built a responsive, audience-focused site from scratch and deployed it to production.
Configured Google Tag Manager with a complete event taxonomy: page views, scroll depth, form submissions, button clicks, and custom conversion events (ticket purchases, PPV signups).
Wired GA4 to capture the full on-site customer journey with custom dimensions for event type, traffic medium, and device category.
Established KPIs and reporting cadence aligned to ticket and PPV revenue goals.



Campaign Analysis & Growth Results
Within two months of launch, the site grew to 3,500+ unique visitors through a combination of organic search, social referral, and direct traffic from fight promotion.
Ongoing analytics work covered:

Channel quality analysis — volume vs. engagement rate by acquisition source (organic, paid, social, direct)
Device-level conversion rates — identifying mobile vs. desktop conversion gaps
Pre- vs. post-event traffic patterns — quantifying the “announcement spike” and measuring decay curves across event cycles
Lead generation funnel — form submission rates for fighter applications and newsletter sign-ups



SEO Strategy

Conducted keyword research aligned to local search intent (gyms, martial arts, events in the target market).
Structured page metadata, heading hierarchy, and internal linking to improve crawlability and topical authority.
Monitored organic impressions and click-through rates in Google Search Console to refine on-page optimizations.







Note



All client metrics and conversion figures are confidential. The analytical approach and pipeline structure are described without proprietary data.


See the GA4 → BigQuery → DuckDB data pipeline and conversion modeling behind this engagement →

section: SEO Competitive Analysis — Trauma Resource Institute
text:
SEO Competitive Analysis — Trauma Resource Institute
I conducted a comprehensive SEO audit for the Trauma Resource Institute (TRI) and benchmarked their performance against key industry competitors.

Approach

Web scraping — collected on-page SEO signals (title tags, meta descriptions, heading structure, page speed proxies, and content length) across TRI and competitor domains.
Keyword research — mapped the competitive keyword landscape for trauma-informed therapy and practitioner training.
Gap analysis — identified content gaps and structural weaknesses relative to competitors ranking for high-intent queries.



Deliverable
An interactive HTML report built in R with Quarto, featuring:

Side-by-side competitor comparison tables
Keyword opportunity visualizations
Prioritized, actionable recommendations for improving TRI’s organic search presence

title: Digital Marketing
section: Enterprise Content Management — Cascade CMS Automation
text:
Enterprise Content Management — Cascade CMS Automation
As part of a web operations engagement, I built a Python-based automation layer on top of the Cascade CMS REST API to transform manual content auditing and bulk publishing into scripted, repeatable processes.

What Was Built

Intelligent API Crawler (discovery.py) — a queue-based crawler that traverses complex folder hierarchies, extracts comprehensive asset metadata, and writes structured CSV inventory reports. Rate-limiting prevents server overload during large-scale crawls.
Headless CLI for AI & Automation (ai_client.py) — a machine-to-machine client designed for automated pipelines and AI-agent consumption. Outputs clean JSON to stdout (parseable by downstream systems) while directing all progress logs to stderr. Handles recursive traversal of deeply nested structuredDataNodes, programmatic workflow resolution, and batch metadata edits across entire sites.



Digital Marketing Impact

Turned multi-hour manual content audits into seconds of script execution.
Enabled AI models and automated scripts to read, modify, and publish CMS content without human intervention — a foundation for scalable content operations.
Delivered a reusable internal tool that reduced operational overhead for ongoing digital content management.

The workshop covered:

Building and segmenting email lists for targeted campaigns
Designing workflows for lead nurturing and re-engagement

Connecting email performance to broader funnel goals

What I Offer
I help marketing teams and organizations build the data infrastructure they need to move from raw event data to reliable, actionable intelligence. My work spans pipeline architecture, analytics implementation, and hands-on team training.

Most marketing analytics problems are actually data infrastructure problems. I design and build pipelines that collect, transform, and deliver clean, reliable data to the tools your team already uses.

title: Teaching
text:
Teaching Philosophy
My teaching philosophy in digital marketing is grounded in the conviction that education must be an active process of learning and becoming by doing — empowering students as emerging professionals rather than passive listeners.
This foundation draws on established learning theory: Vygotsky’s social constructivism frames the classroom as a collaborative community; Gardner’s multiple intelligences honors the diverse ways students understand and process information; and adult motivational theory demonstrates that learners thrive when given autonomy and real-world relevance.
These theories drive my instructional approach. I prioritize project-based learning and authentic assessment over traditional standardized exams. Students tackle hands-on, industry-aligned tasks — developing data-driven marketing campaigns, building analytics dashboards, or consulting for live clients — so they leave with tangible skills and professional portfolios that translate directly to their careers.

title: Teaching
text:
G-TAP
I completed Cal Poly Pomona’s Graduate Teaching Assistant Program (G-TAP), a structured pedagogical training program led by Dr. Ruth Ahn. The program covered evidence-based instructional design, student-centered teaching, and equitable classroom practices.
A key experience was our teaching demonstration, developed collaboratively with fellow graduate students, where I deepened my understanding of the deliberate planning required to build inclusive learning environments — anticipating how students from diverse backgrounds interpret questions, and designing lessons that adapt to them rather than requiring students to conform to a rigid plan.
G-TAP helped me translate personal teaching instincts into formalized, research-backed pedagogy. Understanding the science of how people learn has strengthened both my teaching practice and my own metacognition as a graduate student.



G-TAP Certificate of Completion — Spring 2026

title: Marketing Analytics
section: GA4 → BigQuery → DuckDB Conversion Modeling Pipeline
text:
GA4 → BigQuery → DuckDB Conversion Modeling Pipeline
This covers the data engineering and modeling layer of the Rising Stars engagement. For the website build, GTM/GA4 implementation, and campaign analytics, see Digital Marketing → Rising Stars.
For the Rising Stars Muay Thai engagement, I designed and built a multi-stage data pipeline to process raw GA4 event exports at scale and power downstream predictive modeling.

Pipeline Architecture
GA4 Raw Events
    ↓
BigQuery (Cloud Export)
    ↓
Apache Arrow (In-Memory Transfer)
    ↓
DuckDB (Local Query Engine)
    ↓
Session-Level Aggregations → R Modeling Environment

BigQuery export — automated extraction of raw GA4 event data (sessions, events, user properties, ecommerce) to cloud storage.
GA4 Data API backfill — used the GA4 Data API to recover pre-BigQuery-export data, ensuring complete event-window coverage across both event cycles.
Apache Arrow transfer — zero-copy in-memory transport between cloud and local environments, eliminating intermediate CSV serialization.
DuckDB local engine — SQL-based session-level aggregation, feature engineering (page depth, scroll events, device type, traffic medium), and query optimization for fast iteration during modeling.



Predictive Modeling — Conversion Drivers
Built three logistic regression models — ticket conversion, PPV conversion, and combined conversion — to quantify what independently predicts a purchase.

Features: page depth, device category, traffic medium, pre/post-event timing, content engagement signals
Outputs: odds ratios and average marginal effects for each predictor — giving stakeholders an interpretable answer to “what moves the needle?”
Validation: compared in-sample fit against holdout periods to assess model stability across event cycles







Note



All client metrics, session counts, and conversion figures are confidential. The pipeline architecture and modeling approach are described without proprietary data.

section: Operations Analytics — Ontario International Airport Parking
text:
Operations Analytics — Ontario International Airport Parking
As part of the Cal Poly Pomona CEO Business Challenge, I conducted a multi-year operational time-series analysis for Ontario International Airport (ONT), exploring how parking revenue, passenger volumes, and ride-hailing (TNC) activity interact — with the goal of informing future-proof parking strategy and non-aeronautical revenue growth.

Data Engineering
Working under strict data governance requirements (NDA), I:

Integrated multiple datasets: parking revenue and transactions by lot, passenger counts by airline and direction, TNC trip volumes, and lot occupancy.
Reshaped disparate sources into consistent monthly and weekly time series with engineered date features.
Standardized categories across inconsistent vendor naming conventions.
Generated a non-sensitive YAML schema describing table structures and missingness — enabling safe internal documentation without exposing raw values.

title: Marketing Analytics
section: Geospatial Analytics — Market Area Mapping with Shiny & APIs
text:
Geospatial Analytics — Market Area Mapping with Shiny & APIs
In my role as an Associate Analyst at Robert D. Niehaus, Inc., I replaced a manual, safety-compromised field data collection process with a Shiny R application that automates GPS-based market area delineation for military installations.

The Problem
Determining housing “market areas” for 300+ U.S. military installations previously required analysts to manually note observations at major intersections — a slow, inaccurate, and unsafe process.


The Solution

Strava API integration — the app captures GPS data passively during field drives, eliminating manual recording.
sf + leaflet mapping — automatically generates an interactive map of the driven routes for immediate review and QA.
HERE API integration — provides independent market area estimates as a verification layer against the GPS-driven boundaries.
Deployed as a self-contained Shiny app used operationally across the Housing Market Analysis team.

Impact: eliminated safety risks, improved spatial accuracy, and compressed the field data collection cycle for 300+ installation analyses.
